Neither listed statement describes Habermas’s distinction. Law as an institution is lifeworld law—constitutional basics and the moral core of criminal law—that still needs moral-practical justification and gives binding form to shared communicative expectations. Law as a medium is positivized steering law that organizes markets and administration, drawing legitimacy from the legal order as a whole and carrying systemic imperatives into spheres such as family, school, and social life.

CONFIDENCE: 88
